subject: eurasian sparrowhawk
title: When Its Prey Is Too Big to Kill, This Hawk Holds It Underwater

scenes.text: When this hawk can't kill its prey in the air, it uses water.
The sparrowhawk is a garden hunter, and the female is nearly twice the male's weight.
Normally it grabs small birds and kills them with its talons.
But big prey like magpies fight back.
So birdwatchers have seen sparrowhawks drag their prey into ponds and ditches, and hold it under.
One young female even paddled with her wings to keep a magpie down. Talons failed. Water didn't.

description:
Eurasian sparrowhawks usually kill small birds with their talons, but larger prey such as magpies is sometimes drowned: observers in the Netherlands recorded sparrowhawks holding a starling, a blackbird and a magpie underwater.
Females weigh about 260 g, nearly twice the male's 150 g.
Have you ever seen a hawk hunt in your garden?
first_comment: Female sparrowhawks are up to 25% larger than males, the biggest gap of any bird of prey. Have you seen one at your feeder?
